SCOPING DECISION (stated honestly, not a gap): the mandatory gate is enforced at the ready TRANSITION (validate.check_ready, run by /warp:spec), the canonical point O6's measure names ('the elaboration and validator refuse'). It is deliberately NOT wired into the claimable frontier or plan.py run-check. PLAN-0011's placement gate wired the claim path because its outcome O3 explicitly required 'never claimed for build' (and so touched the fleet area, raising the tier to high); O6 has no such claim-gate language, and wiring it would cross into the fleet area and raise the risk tier without serving O6. So the enforcement is scoped to the ready transition plus a present-only structural check in check_spec.

BACKWARD-COMPAT (RJ6) is achieved by two decisions, not by weakening the rule: (1) the mandatory rule lives in check_ready, never in the run_all/check_spec corpus sweep, so the 121 shipped specs (past ready) are never re-evaluated - identical grandfathering to the placement gate; and (2) an absent behavior_bearing is treated as not behavior-bearing (exempt), so the shipped corpus (which declares no such field) and the existing check_ready selftests (which assert the real WARP-1103 spec and a placed fixture pass check_ready == 0) stay green. The new required-criteria rule is NOT weakened for new behavior-bearing specs (an explicit behavior_bearing: true with no observability is refused).

The C7 soft join is honest: this repository's architecture.yaml declares no observability section (contract_observability reads 'absent'), so the live gate stands down to the spec-level floor; the contract-rules path is proven over temporary contracts in the selftest, and the human-approved architecture contract artifact is deliberately NOT edited (adding a system's observability rules would be a separate human-approved shape change).

The impl is a single commit (observability.py across all engine copies + the edited validate.py/validate_checks.py/capabilities.yaml per copy + the /warp:spec skill per copy + the selftest block + the spec at status review + the regenerated index). Per the review boundary: the spec is at status review (not shipped), no verdict is written, and this proof manifest, .warp/last_verify, and .warp/events.jsonl are left uncommitted. The independent fresh-context reviewer authors the verdict; the orchestrator flips review to shipped on a pass and makes the evidence commit.
rollback: git revert the implementation commit. The change adds one engine organ (.warp/observability.py, synced across the engine), wires it thin from validate_checks.py (check_observability at spec-validation time, observability_gate at the ready transition) and validate.py (one check_observability call in check_spec plus the re-export), asks for the observability classification in the /warp:spec skill, adds one capabilities entry, and adds a selftest block. The mandatory gate is scoped to the ready transition, so it evaluates no already-shipped spec; the present-only structural check stands down for every spec that declares neither field. A spec that declares no behavior_bearing, and a repository with no architecture contract, are unaffected either way (the adoption-safe posture), so there is no migration and nothing to unwind.
